items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Okay. You could do a Doc Cheatham. [INTERVIEWEE] Well you know that’s the thing. I don’t want to do that either.

ctx.x: I know. But well we were just talking about Joe Wilder. And I was introduced to him by Snooky Young. And Snooky and I were together in the Clayton-Hamilton band for 26 years. And he lived to be 90. He played until he passed away. And I just saw how young it kept him. And my dad played and it kept him young. Unless I get to where I can’t play very well you know. But I still feel like I’m really sort of — I feel like there’s a lot more music I want to write and a lot more music I want to play. And I don’t know…
Okay. You could do a Doc Cheatham.
Well you know that’s the thing. I don’t want to do that either. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
